question.problem:
Given that 
${\int }_{1}^{3}f(t)\,\text{d}t=\frac{e}{2}\,i+3e\,j-\,k,$ 
$c=4\,i-j+u\,k,$
and 
${\int }_{1}^{3}c\cdot f(t)\,\text{d}t=0,$ what is the value of $u?$
question.worked_solution:
The dot product rule states that

$$
{\int }_{1}^{3}c\cdot f(t)\,\text{d}t=c\cdot {\int }_{1}^{3}f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

 

Applying the dot-product rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{3}c\cdot f(t)\,\text{d}t & =c\cdot {\int }_{1}^{3}f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =(4\,i-j+u\,k)\cdot (\frac{e}{2}\,i+3e\,j-k) \\  & =2e-3e-u \\  & =-e-u.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since ${\int }_{1}^{3}c\cdot f(t)\,\text{d}t=0,$ we must have $-e-u=0,$ which means that $u=-e.$
